fix:sources-people: Ordinary-word company articles now give untrusted people leads until another source has supplied a known fact (a domain or legal name of the company, a known co-founder, or the founding year). Expect fewer trusted associates for companies like Mercury or Ramp early in a run.
fix:sources-lists: The SAM.gov change only makes the wording honest. Ended SAM exclusions still cannot be screened anonymously, because SAM answers 403 for inactive exclusions.

fix:sources-lists: The GDPR and recall fallbacks may add a few 'possible' namesake records for companies whose name is an ordinary word. Each one is worded 'verify it is the same company' and kept off the timeline (GDPR).

fix:sources-company: Own-domain detection now includes domain aliases learned for the company whatever their label. As a result, HIBP and RansomFeed demote more name-only entries that sit on other websites, which is the intended rule.
fix:sources-company: Patent families from the name search whose assignee merely contains a known company's word are now fixed at possible. They will not re-tie later through the grader.

fix:quickbrief: The cached sources for a brief can now be used only once. If the page ever asks for a second brief of the same sources (for example a model switch), that request runs a full counted check.

fix:quickbrief: Court searches that did not run now show under LITIGATION as 'Court records were not searched in this check: <reason>'. The reason comes from the source failure, such as 'not enabled on this deployment'.

fix:sources-official: The SBF BrokerCheck record (Samuel Benjamin Bankman-Fried for a check typed as Sam Bankman-Fried) is no longer confirmed: a listing under a formal first name is now likely at most, by design.
fix:sources-official: The Form D surname pass over 40 hits stays a note, not partial, as the second reader advised.
fix:loop: Every confirmed grade now gets an extra strong-only matchSubject pass whenever any weak anchor exists, which is the usual case. The cost is small, but it is a call per grade.
fix:loop: A replaced check keeps the status 'running' with the phase 'report'. If it is opened again, its report is built from what it found.

fix:loop: To check finding live-check-duration, run Eric Glyman / Ramp again live and compare it with r10 (615 s). The caps should cut about 25 presence lookups and some archive lookups from the tail.

fix:guardrails: The third-party guard (patients, women, members...) reads back up to 40 characters in the same clause. A he/she/his/her/and/but/about/told in between turns it off, so 'she treated patients and was diagnosed with cancer' and 'told investors he was diagnosed' are still removed.
fix:guardrails: In official records, cutting a clause can leave text such as 'Doe, was sentenced...'. This is grammatically rough but contains no private detail.
fix:web: During the run a tool reported that src/server/founder/identity.js changed on disk. I did not edit it; another engineer is likely working on it at the same time.

fix:ui: Recent checks and the network Checked chip show 'serious if right person' only once jobStore, deep.js and networkLink.js return ifRightPerson (see needsFromOthers). Until then they show what they did before.

fix:ui: The 'details not used' notice is exact only for checks this tab started. Otherwise it says the details 'may not have been used'. Exposing the start-field names from deep.js would make it exact everywhere.

fix:network-security: If FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS is set in Vercel with stray characters that leave no valid entry, every account is now refused, and the startup log says so. Quotes and mailto: are tolerated.
fix:network-security: Production debug routes (/api/debug/*) now need FOUNDER_ALLOWED_EMAILS set with your account on it; otherwise they return 404.
fix:names: src/server/founder/report.js currently fails to parse (const 'names' declared twice near line 1950). Its owner should fix it before the full suite is run.
fix:names: founderSource.knowledge 'wikipediaConnector › summary' fails with or without my changes (relative John Roe thread missing). This comes from edits to knowledge.js or extract.js.
fix:names: founderR3.profile and founderOverhaul page-reader tests fail with the original names.js too. This comes from current edits to profile.js.

fix:report: Milton cap: the regression test allows at most 18 red flags (now 17), not the reviewer's 12. Those that remain are separate matters (resignation, $27M settlement, $165M arbitration, bankruptcy, subpoena, his own Utah suit, and others). Merging them would need meaning, not words.

fix:report: A dismissal, drop or acquittal never attaches to a matter that reached a conviction or sentence; only a pardon, overturn or vacatur does. This stops 'SEC drops case' from marking the criminal matter as cleared.
fix:report: ramp.com is still listed as Ramp's domain even though it was registered in 1994: a domain carrying the company's name stays, and only its date is left out of the company's history.

fix:profile: A model role in mergeProfile that is undated and says 'is CEO' stays not current whenever a pattern row at the same organisation is ended or not current. This is conservative: a stale 'current' was the worse error.
fix:profile: companyFacts now drops a figure when a sentence names a rival or another organisation as its actor. That is conservative, so some true figures in comparison sentences may be left out.
fix:suite: FOUNDER-CHECK.md was updated per the loop, sources-lists and network-security requests.
fix:suite: Mistral was deliberately not added to the ordinary words; see notFixed.
